$what-an-entry-is: A licence for ONE test, keyed by its TEST NAME, to fail without failing CI.
$rules: A failure that is NOT on this list fails the gate. That is the whole point of the gate.
The list may only SHRINK. If a listed test PASSES, the gate fails until the entry is deleted — so a fix and its deletion land in the same PR.

Every reason must name a mechanism: what the test binds, spawns, writes, reads, or assumes about the machine or the calendar. The loader REJECTS the words 'flaky', 'intermittent' and 'unstable' — a failure with no named mechanism is indistinguishable from a real regression, which is how a real regression hides.

A test that is genuinely nondeterministic cannot satisfy the shrink-only ratchet, so it may set "nondeterministic": true to opt out of it. That is a bigger licence and costs more: such an entry MUST carry "tracking" (the issue where the defect is being fixed) and "expires" (an ISO date after which the gate fails). A quarantine with no meter is a parking space. The meter also has a MAXIMUM READING: "expires" may be at most 180 days out. An expiry that merely parses is not a ceiling — 2099-01-01 parses — and "nondeterministic" plus a far-future date is a permanent exemption with the paperwork filled in. Past two quarters it is not a quarantine, it is a decision to stop testing the thing, and that belongs in a PR someone reviews.

A SKIPPED test is neither a pass nor a fail, and the ratchet treats it as neither. An allowlisted test that skips KEEPS its entry — it was not exercised, so nothing was learned, so nothing changes; the gate prints it under NOTE rather than instructing you to delete it. This is not hypothetical: PW-9 below runs only where pwsh is on PATH, ubuntu-latest's pwsh availability has moved within one image label, and reading that skip as a pass would tell you to delete a quarantine for a test that still fails every time pwsh is present. Skips also do NOT count toward the gate's minimum-tests floor, which is measured on EXECUTED tests; and every skipped name is printed on every run, so a test that quietly stops executing on the runner is a one-line diff between two job logs.

$fields.test: the test name exactly as the runner reports it — this is the key
$fields.file: repo-relative path. CHECKED STATICALLY on every node version: it must be one of the files package.json scripts.test selects, so an entry cannot outlive a rename. Additionally cross-checked against the runner's own attribution on the node versions that report it (node 25 and 26 do — CI pins 26 since #101; node 22 does not).
$fields.reason: the mechanism — at least 40 characters, and not the word 'flaky'
$fields.nondeterministic: optional; true opts the entry out of the shrink-only ratchet
$fields.tracking: required when nondeterministic — the issue tracking the fix
$fields.expires: required when nondeterministic — ISO date. A date-only value is licensed THROUGH the end of that UTC day, and may be at most 180 days from now

entries.$why-nondeterministic: Not the assertion — that is deterministic. What varies is whether the test RUNS AT ALL: it is gated on pwsh being on PATH, and ubuntu-latest's pwsh availability is not stable run to run. Demonstrated minutes apart on the same image label (Image: ubuntu-24.04): run 35902475340 had pwsh (PW-8/PW-9/W-4 executed, PW-9 failed, gate PASS) and run 35902484923 did not (all three SKIPPED, so PW-9 counted as not-failing and the shrink-only ratchet failed the gate with 'PASSED this run'). A deterministic entry therefore cannot hold: with pwsh the gate needs the entry, without it the gate rejects it. Quarantining is the designed answer. The alternative is to make the runner deterministic — pin the image or install pwsh in .github/workflows/test.yml — which is a change to the gate itself and belongs with whoever owns it.
entries.reason: DETERMINED, and deliberately still listed. Runs only where pwsh is on PATH, which ubuntu-latest sometimes has and a typical macOS checkout does not, so it skips locally and usually runs in CI. `exit 7` is a PowerShell LANGUAGE statement, not a native exit status: inside `& { ... }` it terminates the whole host before the __DFW_END_ sentinel line executes, so stdout is empty. Probed against pwsh 7.4.2 (mcr.microsoft.com/powershell) on 2026-09-23: (a) `try { & { exit 7 } } finally { ... }` DOES run the finally, so the sentinel CAN be made to survive, but $LASTEXITCODE is empty there and execution still stops afterwards; (b) a separate runspace ([powershell]::Create().AddScript('exit 7').Invoke()) survives the host but also yields no exit code, in the runspace or outside it; (c) only a CHILD pwsh (`& pwsh -NoProfile -Command <cmd>`) sets $LASTEXITCODE to 7. So PowerShell exposes the value passed to `exit` to nothing in-session, and the only fix is to run every dispatch in a child process — which ends the long-lived session that is the daemon's entire purpose: cwd, PowerShell variables, functions, aliases and any $env: the command sets would stop persisting across dispatches (env flows parent to child only). Reporting one exit code correctly is not worth losing session state, so the gap stands and the test stays red rather than being weakened to match it. Note the same statement has the same effect in bash — `{ exit 7 ; }` exits that shell too — so this is a limitation of the in-session sentinel protocol, not of wrappers/powershell.cjs specifically; there is simply no bash test asserting it. Issue #95.

$why-the-key-is-the-name: Not file::name, which was the first design. node 22's junit reporter emits no testcase file attribute and node 25's does, so a file-based key resolves differently on a developer's machine and on the runner — the list would appear to shrink locally and silently fail to match in CI. The name is identical on every version. The cost is ambiguity, and it is paid explicitly: the gate FAILS when a listed name matches more than one test in the run.
$environment: This list describes the GATE's environment: ubuntu-latest + node 26, as pinned in .github/workflows/test.yml (raised from 22 by #101 — node 22 and 24 exit 0 when a describe-scoped after() hook throws, so that failure class was invisible to the gate). ONE entry remains (PW-9) and it is platform-specific: it runs only where pwsh is on PATH, so on a typical macOS checkout it SKIPS — which the ratchet now leaves alone rather than reading as a pass. That change matters here specifically, because ubuntu-latest's own pwsh availability is not stable run to run. The reverse direction is the trap: a Linux-only failure is invisible on a macOS checkout. `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src:ro node:26 bash -c 'cp -a /src /repo && cd /repo && rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && node --test <file>'` reproduces the runner's bash 5.2 / readline 8.1 environment locally — that is how the five bracketed-paste entries were reproduced and cleared, and it is the recipe to reach for before assuming a CI-only failure is a flake.
